Ginnungagap:
===Etymology===
Compound of {{com|non||alt1=ginnunga|gap|t2=gap, empty space}}. The first element is of uncertain origin and meaning and has been explained in a number of ways. (1) It is related to {{cog|gem-pro|*ginnaną}}, from which {{m|gem-pro|*biginnaną||to begin}} descended, thus meaning "primeval". (2) The prefix {{m|non|ginn-}} (for instance in {{m|non|ginnheilagr||most holy}}, used of the supreme gods), therefore giving the meaning "mighty, vast". (3) Old Norse {{m|non|gína||to gape; to be astonished}} + {{m|non|-ung||forms verbal nouns from verbs; -ation; -ing}}, i.e. "gap of the gapings" or similar. (4) A genitive plural of {{m|non|ginnungr||hawk}}, which would give an air-kenning "hawk-gap" referring to the midspace between earth and heaven. This sense is attested by Snorre, who gives {{m|non|ginnungagap}} as a synonym for "air", and supported by the sky-kenning ''ginnunga vé'' "mansions of hawks" as found in {{w|Haustlǫng}}.

====Usage notes====
Old Norse makes the distinction between ''hof'' "a hall, a sanctuary with a roof" and {{m|non|hǫrgr||an altar, any cult site without a roof}}.
The prevalent meaning of ''hof'' in Old Norse literature is “temple, sanctuary”. Cleasby and Vigfússon (1874) note the generic meaning "''a hall'' (as in German and Saxon)" in {{w|Hymiskviða}} 33 as a ''hapax legomenon''. The meaning of “court” follows Middle High German and appears only from the 14th century and almost exclusively in compounds such as {{m|non|hofferð|hof-ferð|pride, pomp}}, {{m|non|hofgarðr|hof-garðr|lordly mansion}}, {{m|non|hoffolk|hof-folk|courtiers}}.

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|non|gmq-pro|ᚾᛁ}}, from {{inh|non|gem-pro|*ne}}, from {{inh|non|ine-pro|*né|t=not}}. The word can be seen in fossilized prefixes such as {{m|non|nǫkkurr}}, {{m|non|neinn}} (né einn). It is still part of the core lexicon in modern Icelandic, it is used when negating conjunctions similar to {{m+|en|nor}}. Its cognates in the Old West/East Germanic languages are {{cog|ang|ne}}, {{cog|ofs|ne}}, {{m|ofs|ni}}, {{cog|osx|ne}}, {{m|osx|ni}}, {{cog|odt|ne}}, {{cog|goh|ni}}, {{cog|got|𐌽𐌹}}.
